article.text: The official voter list isn't searchable. That's the whole problem.

Download any electoral roll from a state CEO website and you get a PDF of scanned images. Ctrl+F finds nothing, copy-paste returns nothing and the text is often in Punjabi, Bengali or Tamil script that ordinary converters can't read. We turn those PDFs into a searchable voter list in Excel: one booth per sheet, one voter per row, with every name in the original script plus English and Hindi.

Looking for an Excel voter list you can filter, sort and search in seconds? You're in the right place. Below: what's in the file, how we build it and how to get one for any state, district, assembly or Lok Sabha constituency in India.
What Is a Voter List in Excel?
A voter list (officially the electoral roll ) is the Election Commission of India's record of every registered voter in a constituency. It's split into parts and each part is one polling booth.
A voter list in Excel is that same official roll, rebuilt as a spreadsheet:
(Sample row for illustration. Relative names, section and polling station follow in the next columns.)
Nothing is invented. Every field comes from the published roll, organised so your team can actually search it.
Why You Need a Searchable Voter List (Not a Scanned PDF)

Here's the scale of the problem, using Punjab as an example. The 2022 Assembly election had 2,16,09,482 electors across 24,740 polling stations, an average of 873 voters per booth. At about 30 voters per page, that's roughly 29 pages per booth and over 7 lakh pages for the state.
(Source: ECI statistical report, Punjab Assembly Election 2022.)
Nobody reads that. Here's how the three options compare:
The ECI portal is fine for checking whether you are registered. A campaign needs to see everyone at once and for that, the searchable voter list is the Excel one.
Who Buys Excel Voter Lists

items: Candidates and campaign managers. Booth-wise voter counts, gender splits and age brackets. That's the base of every booth plan.
Booth-level workers (BLAs, panna pramukhs). A walk list for their own booth, sorted by section and house number.
Political consultants and survey agencies. Sampling frames and demographic weights. First-time voters per booth take one filter.
Parties tracking roll revisions. After a Summary Revision or Special Intensive Revision, match the old Excel voter list to the new one by EPIC number and see every addition and deletion.
Researchers and journalists. Gender ratios, age pyramids and checks for inflated rolls, all of which need structured data.
Election software users. Booth-management apps and CRMs import Excel or CSV and the English columns import cleanly.

article.text: Hindi, English and Regional Language Voter Lists in Excel

India's rolls are printed in more than a dozen scripts. That's fine for a local booth worker. It's a real problem for a consultant in Delhi handling a seat in Bengal, or for a CRM that only accepts Roman letters.
So every file, for every state, has three versions of each name:

items: → Original script, exactly as printed in the official roll: Gurmukhi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Odia, Marathi and so on
→ English transliteration, for software imports, English-speaking teams and sorting A–Z
→ Hindi (Devanagari) transliteration, for Hindi-speaking field teams working in any state

article.text: The transliteration is reviewed by people, not just run through a tool. Machine transliteration mangles Indian names more often than you'd think (Kaur, Kour and Kor are a classic Punjab mess). A person checks every file before it ships.
The result: a Hindi voter list in Excel and an English voter list in Excel in the same file, with no extra order needed.
How We Convert Voter List PDFs to Excel
This is where ordinary PDF-to-Excel converters fail on voter lists and why we built our own pipeline.

items: Get the official roll. We download the latest final roll from the state CEO website or the ECI voter services portal. We never use third-party copies.
Merge the supplementary lists. Additions, deletions and corrections published after the base roll are applied, so you get the roll as it stands today.
Remove non-voter pages. Cover pages and maps are set aside, but we keep the official summary totals for checking.
Straighten and sharpen every page. Tilted, faint scans are the main cause of OCR errors.
Detect each voter box. About 30 boxes per page, each cut out separately so no field bleeds into the next voter's.
Run OCR tuned to the script. Gurmukhi, Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, English and more.
Split into columns. EPIC, name, relative, relation, house number, age, gender and section each get their own column.
Transliterate and review. English and Hindi versions are added and then checked by hand.
Check against the official booth summary. Row counts and male/female totals must match what the roll says for that part.

article.text: Could you do this yourself? For a few pages, sure. For a constituency of 250+ booths, you'll spend weeks building a pipeline before you see a single usable row. We've already run a full state's roll through it this year.
What's in Your Excel Voter List
Every assembly or Lok Sabha constituency comes as one Excel workbook:

items: A summary sheet: every booth with part number, polling station name and total, male, female and third-gender voters
One sheet per booth, named by part number (Part 1, Part 2, …), so each booth worker gets only their own voters
A header on every booth sheet with constituency name and number, part number, polling station and roll date
Section and street names, so you can plan routes street by street, not just booth by booth
The Part No. column on every row, so nothing is lost if you combine sheets

article.text: Want a different format? We can send CSV or a single merged sheet on request. District and state orders arrive as one workbook per constituency, in folders named by district.
How to Search a Voter List in Excel (6 Tricks)

items: Search the whole constituency at once: press Ctrl+F → Options → set Within: Workbook → Find All. You'll see every matching name or EPIC number across all booth sheets, with the booth it's on.
Jump to any booth: right-click the sheet arrows at the bottom-left of Excel and pick the part number.
Build a door-to-door walk list: in the booth sheet, sort by Section, then by House No.
Find first-time voters: filter the Age column to Less than or equal to 19.
Group families: sort by House No., then by Relative Name and households line up together.
Analyse the whole constituency: use Data → Get Data → From Workbook (Power Query) to stack every booth sheet into one table, then pivot any way you like. Or ask us for the merged-sheet version.

article.text: 99% Accuracy and How We Check It
We won't claim 100%. Nobody running OCR on scanned government PDFs gets 100% and a seller who says they do hasn't checked. Our files come in at 99% field accuracy and here's how we keep them there:

items: Row counts must match each booth's official summary. A booth that fails doesn't ship.
EPIC numbers are checked against the standard format and anything unusual is reviewed by hand.
Ages outside 18–120 are treated as misreads and corrected.
Gender totals must match the official male and female counts per booth.
Transliterations are reviewed by people before delivery.

Let's be clear about what's in these files and what isn't.

What's in: only the information printed in the publicly available electoral roll (EPIC number, name, relative's name, house number, age, gender, section, part number and polling station), plus our transliterations of that same text.

article.text: Andhra Pradesh just deleted one voter in ten.

That's not a typo. The Special Intensive Revision of 2026 took AP's roll from 4,16,27,694 names down to 3,72,02,684 in the draft published on 31 July — the biggest clean-up the state has seen in more than two decades. Then it added 3,933 new polling booths on top.

If your campaign is still working off 2024 data, you're planning on a roll that no longer exists. Below: what changed, why it breaks old booth plans, and how to get the Andhra Pradesh voter list in Excel — one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every name in Telugu, English and Hindi.
45 Lakh Names Gone: What SIR 2026 Did to the AP Roll
Booth Level Officers went door to door through June and July 2026. Anyone they couldn't verify didn't make the draft.

One more number jumps out. The draft has 1,89,30,929 women and 1,82,69,019 men — about 1,036 women for every 1,000 men. Few large states can say that. If your outreach plan assumes a male-majority electorate, it's wrong here.
Claims and objections closed on 30 August, and the final roll was scheduled for 3 October 2026. That final roll is what goes into our files.
Your 2024 Booth Data Is Now Pointing at the Wrong Doors
The deletions grab the headlines. The booth changes do the quiet damage.
SIR capped every polling station at 1,200 voters, which pushed AP from 46,397 booths to 50,330. Every split sets off a chain reaction:

items: Part numbers shift — old booth 142 becomes 142 and 143, and everything after it renumbers
Voters move to a different building, sometimes a different school down the road
Your 2024 walk list now sends volunteers to the wrong streets
Booth-wise past results stop lining up with the new parts

article.text: Here's a ten-second test. Count the booths for any constituency in your old file, then count them in the new roll. Different numbers? Then every booth-level report you built needs rebuilding — no shortcut.
Telugu Names Break Ordinary Converters
We've watched off-the-shelf PDF-to-Excel tools choke on AP rolls, and it's always the same three problems.

The family name comes first. Telugu puts the *intiperu* up front — Kondapalli (family) Srinivasa Rao (given name). The same man signs as "K. Srinivasa Rao" in English. We keep the printed order, so sorting by name lines up whole households.

One name, half a dozen spellings. Venkata or Venkat. Lakshmi or Laxmi. Naidu or Nayudu. Let a machine guess and it picks differently every time — and your search quietly stops working. A person on our team reviews every transliteration so one spelling holds across the file.

The script itself fights back. Telugu's rounded letters and stacked consonants (ఒత్తులు) smear on a scanned page. Miss one cluster and a name becomes someone else's. Every booth gets checked against the official men and women totals before it leaves us.
(Sample row for illustration.)
What Lands in Your Inbox
One Excel workbook per assembly constituency, and inside it:

items: A summary sheet — every booth, its polling station, and men, women and third-gender totals
One sheet per booth, named by part number, with polling station and section names up top
One row per voter: EPIC number, name, relative's name, relation, house number, age, gender, section
Names in Telugu, English and Hindi
Supplementary lists merged in, deleted voters flagged — not silently mixed in
Public roll data only. No phone numbers. No photos. No caste tags.

article.text: Need CSV or one merged sheet for your campaign software? Just ask when you order. The voter list in Excel guide shows how to search the files.
Andhra Pradesh by the Numbers

AP had 4,13,33,702 voters on the roll at the 2024 election, with turnout above 80%. The SIR draft dropped below even the 2019 figure of 3.94 crore. Put simply: AP's real turnout was higher than the official percentage suggested, because the old denominator was padded with names that weren't really there.

article.text: In Arunachal, reaching a booth can take a full day on foot. The voter list shouldn't take a week.

Sixty constituencies sounds small. It isn't — not when polling stations sit across river crossings, ridge lines and border villages, some serving just a few dozen voters. Campaign teams here don't get second trips. They need to know exactly who's on each booth's list before anyone sets out.
That's what the Arunachal Pradesh voter list in Excel gives you: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in English and Hindi.
Small Booths, Long Walks, No Room for Guesswork

Think about what a 40-voter booth means. Forty people. A campaign can plan for every single one of them — names, families, ages — but only if the list is sitting in a sheet you can sort, not buried in a scanned PDF on page 3 of 4.
Our clients in hill states tell us the same thing: the expensive mistake isn't missing a big booth. It's sending a team six hours up a valley with the wrong list.
SIR 2026 Rewrote the Roll
Arunachal was in phase three of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers went house to house, the draft came out in July 2026, and the final roll was scheduled for 22 September 2026.
What changed on the ground:

items: Names of voters who died, moved away or were registered twice — removed
Young voters who turned 18 by the 1 July 2026 qualifying date — added

Here's the trap: the Arunachal roll is printed in English, so people assume conversion is a breeze. It isn't.

article.text: Got Assam voter data from 2021? It's mapped to constituencies that don't exist anymore.

The 2023 delimitation redrew the state. Still 126 assembly seats, still 14 Lok Sabha seats — but boundaries moved, some constituencies were renamed, a few were abolished and new ones appeared. Reserved seats changed too. A booth that sat in one constituency in 2021 can sit in a completely different one today.

We provide the Assam voter list in Excel on the current boundaries: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in Assamese or Bengali as printed, plus English and Hindi.
Old Assam Data Is Mapped to a Map That's Gone
Here's how the 2023 changes break old files:

items: Totals don't compare. A constituency's 2021 voter count covers different ground than its 2026 count.
Reserved seats shifted — Assam now has 19 ST and 9 SC seats, up from 16 and 8.
Booth-to-constituency mapping changed, so old booth-wise analysis lands in the wrong seat.
The roll itself was refreshed by a Special Revision ahead of the 2026 election, with the final roll out in February 2026.

article.text: Trying to patch an old file to the new map is an ugly workaround. Start from the current roll instead.
Three Scripts, One File
Assam is one of the toughest states we convert. The roll isn't in one language.
Assamese covers most of the Brahmaputra Valley — and Assamese has letters of its own, ৰ (ra) and ৱ (wa), that standard Bengali OCR gets wrong every time. We run OCR set up for Assamese specifically.
Bengali is used in the Barak Valley districts. Same script family, different letters, different spellings.
English shows up in some areas too.
Whatever your constituency is printed in, the file keeps it — and adds English and Hindi so a consultant in Guwahati and a volunteer from Delhi can work off the same sheet.
(Sample row for illustration.)
Surnames are their own headache: Bora or Borah, Baruah or Barua. We transliterate exactly what's printed and keep the spelling consistent across the file, so your search actually finds people.

article.text: Bihar was the guinea pig. Every other state is now catching up.

In mid-2025, Bihar became the first state to go through the Special Intensive Revision — Booth Level Officers rebuilding the roll door to door across all 243 constituencies. Lakhs of dead, migrated and duplicate entries came off the draft. Lakhs of new and returning voters came back on through claims. The final SIR roll landed on 30 September 2025, and that's the roll Bihar voted on in November.

So if your booth data dates from 2020, or even the 2024 Lok Sabha poll, it was built on a roll that's been torn down and rebuilt. The Bihar voter list in Excel from Setuk.org uses the SIR roll: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
Bihar Went First – and Its Old Lists Went Stale
This wasn't a routine annual update. Voters had to hand in enumeration forms, and anyone who couldn't be verified didn't make the draft. Three things happened at once:

items: Old entries vanished — voters who'd died, moved for work and registered elsewhere, or appeared twice
New entries came in through claims and objections before the final roll
Booth lists got reorganised across many constituencies

article.text: Bihar sends a huge share of its workforce to other states. That's exactly why the old roll was padded — and why a 2020 walk list now sends volunteers looking for people who aren't there.
Hindi Rolls Aren't as Easy as They Look
People assume a Hindi roll converts cleanly. Then they open the output.

The scans are the problem. Matras and joined letters blur, and OCR starts swapping ि for ी, श for ष. "Kumari" turns into two different names in two different booths. The same name gets written as Kumar, Kr. and Kumaar across a constituency — and your search finds a third of them.

We fix that by hand. Every name gets a consistent Hindi spelling and an English transliteration, so the file works in CRMs and campaign apps that choke on Devanagari, and for consultants who'd rather read Roman script. Each booth is checked against the official men and women totals before it ships.

article.text: Goa votes in early 2027. In a state this small, that's tomorrow.

Goa's 40 constituencies are tiny by Indian standards — a few tens of thousands of voters each. Results are routinely decided by a few hundred votes, sometimes fewer. Every household, every new voter, every family that moved from one village to the next actually counts.
The Goa voter list in Excel gives you every one of them in a sheet you can work with: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, searchable by name or EPIC number.
In Goa, Elections Are Won by Hundreds of Votes
When a seat can swing on 300 votes, you can't run a campaign on estimates. You need to know:

items: which booths carry the most voters
which families are new on the roll since 2022
where first-time voters are clustered
which names came off the roll in the revision — and whether they should have

article.text: All of that sits in the roll. None of it is usable while it's a stack of scanned PDFs.
The SIR 2026 Roll Is the 2027 Roll
Goa went through phase two of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers verified voters house to house from November 2025, and the final roll was published on 21 February 2026.
Continuous updates will add new voters before polling day. But the SIR roll is the foundation — the 2022 roll no longer matches it booth for booth. Plan 2027 on the 2026 roll.
Apostrophes, Accents and Other Search Killers
Goa's names are a nightmare for software. Not because they're unusual — because they're written so many ways.

D'Souza, De Souza, Dsouza. Fernandes, Fernandez. Rodrigues, Rodriguez. Pereira, Periera. One family can show up spelt three ways in three booths, and an apostrophe alone is enough to make a search miss. Konkani and Marathi names bring their own variations on top.
We keep each name exactly as printed and make the spelling consistent within your file, so a search for one form finds the voter. Every file also gets English and Hindi columns.

They're all there — as Rameshbhai. Same with Kokila, who's on the roll as Kokilaben. It's a tiny detail, and it quietly wrecks every quick search, every mail merge and every "find this voter" request a campaign office fields in a day.

December 2027 Is Closer Than It Looks
Gujarat's next Assembly election is due in late 2027. The roll it'll be fought on was rebuilt in phase two of the Special Intensive Revision, with the final version published on 17 February 2026.
That gives teams roughly a year and a half of runway. Here's how the good ones use it:

items: Map every booth on the SIR roll, not the 2022 one
Flag first-time voters — anyone 18 or 19 on the 2026 roll
Size each booth and assign workers in proportion
Re-check after each continuous-update supplement

article.text: Steps one and two are impossible from PDFs and take minutes from a sheet.
-bhai, -ben and the Three-Part Name
Gujarati rolls follow a pattern most software doesn't expect:
Given name + suffix · father's or husband's name · surname

items: *Rameshbhai Kantilal Patel*
*Kokilaben Rameshbhai Shah*

Why Gujarati Rolls Break Hindi-Trained OCR

Gujarati looks like Devanagari without the line on top — and that missing line (*shirorekha*) is exactly what Hindi-trained OCR uses to find where words begin and end. Run a Gujarati roll through a Hindi tool and you get broken words and misread letters.
We use OCR set up for Gujarati, then check every booth against the official men and women totals.

article.text: Haryana's new voter list is barely out. Most campaigns haven't even opened it yet.

The Special Intensive Revision's final roll for Haryana was scheduled for 3 October 2026 — the first fully re-verified roll since the 2024 Assembly election. Every booth plan, every panna-level worksheet, every list of "our" voters built before this needs checking against it.
The Haryana voter list in Excel gives you the new roll ready to work: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
Haryana's New Roll Is Fresh Off the Press

Booth Level Officers went house to house in mid-2026 under phase three of SIR. The draft came out at the end of July, claims ran through August and September, and the final roll followed. What that did to the data:

items: deceased voters removed
duplicate entries — people registered in two places — cleaned out
voters who had shifted away taken off their old booth
new 18-year-olds added, using 1 July 2026 as the qualifying date
booth lists rebalanced where polling stations were split or merged
the 2024 roll stopped matching the 2026 one, booth for booth

article.text: The NCR Problem: Voters Who Moved Without Telling Anyone

Here's where Haryana is different. A big chunk of the state sits in the National Capital Region — Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Jhajjar, Panipat — where people move flats, cities and jobs constantly. Plenty of them never updated their voter entry.

SIR caught a lot of that. In NCR constituencies, expect bigger swings in who's on each booth than in rural Haryana. If you're running a campaign in Gurugram or Faridabad, the old list is especially stale.

Snow closes passes for months. Some booths sit at the end of a day's drive and a long walk. A campaign that plans its ground in summer 2027 will find half its high-altitude booths unreachable until it's too late. The teams that do well start mapping a year or more out.

article.text: In Bengaluru, a voter list goes stale faster than milk.

People rent, move, change jobs, move again. Half of them never touch their voter registration. So a Bengaluru booth list from 2023 is full of people who've long since left — and missing the ones who arrived. Every campaign in the city knows it. Few have a clean fix.

The Special Intensive Revision is the fix. Karnataka's SIR final roll was scheduled for 27 October 2026, and the Karnataka voter list in Excel gives it to you ready to use: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Kannada, English and Hindi.
Bengaluru Moves Faster Than Its Voter List

Bengaluru's 28 assembly seats are a different world from rural Karnataka. Apartment blocks where half the flats changed hands since the last election. PG accommodations where nobody stays more than a year. Old layouts where the house numbering itself changed.

SIR sent Booth Level Officers to all of them. Expect big swings — people removed as "shifted", new residents added — in city constituencies. If you're campaigning in Bengaluru, last election's list isn't a starting point. It's a trap.
SIR 2026: The Final Roll Is Weeks Away
Karnataka is in phase three. The draft roll came out in late August 2026, claims ran into October, and the final roll follows. Across the state:

items: deceased voters removed
shifted voters taken off their old booth
duplicates cleaned out
new voters added — 1 October 2026 is the qualifying date
booths over 1,200 voters split, and part numbers changed
Bengaluru's rental-heavy seats see the biggest swings of all

article.text: The 2023 Assembly roll and the 2024 Lok Sabha roll both stop lining up.
Initials, Village Names and Vowel Endings
Kannada names don't behave the way software expects. We see three patterns trip people up constantly:
Initials up front. H. D., K. R., B. S. — usually the village or family name and the father's name. Two voters with the same given name can only be told apart by them, so we never drop them.
Vowel endings. The roll says *Manjunatha*; everyday English says *Manjunath*. We keep the printed form, so your search should use the first few letters.
Script quirks. Kannada's rounded letters and stacked consonants blur on scans, and OCR mistakes ಬ for ಭ more often than you'd think. Every booth is checked against the official men and women totals.

article.text: Most states number their houses. Kerala names them.

Open a Kerala roll and next to a voter you'll often find a house name — *Thekkedath*, *Puthenveedu*, *Kizhakkethil* — where other states print "14/2". It tells you which household a voter belongs to better than any number could. And generic converters throw it away, or mash it into the name column.
We keep it. The Kerala voter list in Excel comes as one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, with house names intact and names in Malayalam, English and Hindi.
Kerala Doesn't Number Its Houses – It Names Them
Why this matters on the ground:

items: Sort a booth by house name and whole families line up — grandparents, parents, adult children
Spot households where several members are new on the roll
Plan door-to-door visits by tharavad, not by guesswork
Match voters to the names your local workers actually use

article.text: House names are also how people find each other in Kerala. "Which Anil?" — "Anil from Puthenveedu." Your file should speak the same language.
Chillu Letters: Where Malayalam OCR Breaks

Malayalam has a set of letters called chillu — ൽ, ൻ, ർ, ൾ, ൺ — consonants without the vowel attached. They're everywhere in names (അനിൽ, Anil), and they're the single most common place Malayalam OCR goes wrong on a scan.
Get one chillu wrong and the name changes. That's why every Kerala file gets a person checking names, and every booth is matched against the official men and women totals.
(Sample row for illustration.)
The SIR 2026 Roll

Kerala went through phase two of the Special Intensive Revision. The final roll was published on 21 February 2026 and used for the 2026 Assembly election. The revision cleaned out deceased and shifted voters and duplicates, and added new voters.
Kerala also has more overseas electors than any other state — Gulf migration does that. They're registered under Form 6A and form part of the roll.

article.text: Madhya Pradesh has 230 assembly seats. Try downloading them one booth at a time.

Each constituency's roll comes as a few hundred separate PDFs. Multiply that across the state and you're looking at tens of thousands of files of scanned Hindi text — none of it searchable. A state war room that wants to compare booths across Malwa, Mahakaushal, Bundelkhand and Chambal can't do it from that.
The Madhya Pradesh voter list in Excel turns the whole thing into data: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
230 Seats Is a Lot of PDFs
Here's what a state-level team actually needs from a voter list:

items: booth sizes across every constituency, side by side
first-time voters in each district
the gender split, booth by booth
which booths were split or renumbered in the revision
one consistent format, so 230 files open the same way
something analysts can load into software without a week of cleanup
a Lok Sabha view, combining segments

article.text: Seven things. All of them take minutes from a sheet and are basically impossible from PDFs.
What SIR 2026 Changed
Madhya Pradesh was part of phase two of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers went door to door from November 2025, and the final roll was published in February 2026.

Deceased, shifted and duplicate entries came off. New voters came on. Booth lists were tidied, and some polling stations were split. The roll MP voted on in 2023 doesn't line up booth for booth with the 2026 one — and the 2026 roll is the one heading into 2028.
47 Tribal Seats – More Than Any Other State
Forty-seven of MP's seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribe candidates — across Jhabua, Alirajpur, Dhar, Barwani, Mandla, Dindori, Shahdol and more. That's more ST seats than any other state in India.

In these constituencies, names written in Devanagari on the roll have no fixed English spelling. Bhuria or Bhuriya. Markam or Markaam. One person picks one consistent English form per name across the file, so your search finds everyone.

*Sunil Ramesh Patil.* That middle name is his father's. For a married woman — *Sunita Sunil Patil* — it's her husband's. items: group a booth into households in one sort
spot when a woman's entry still carries her father's name — a sign the record pre-dates her marriage

article.text: SIR 2026 Hits Mumbai Hardest
Maharashtra is in phase three of the Special Intensive Revision; the final roll was scheduled for 27 October 2026. Rural seats will see the usual clean-up — deaths, duplicates, people who moved.

Mumbai, Thane, Pune and the other big cities are a different story. Tenants move every year or two. Redevelopment pulls whole buildings' worth of voters out at once. Migrants come and go. SIR caught a lot of that — so in urban constituencies, expect big differences between the 2024 roll and the 2026 one. Plan on the new roll, especially for city wards.
ळ and Other Things Hindi OCR Can't Read
Marathi is written in Devanagari, so people assume a Hindi tool will handle it. Close — but not close enough.

ळ (the retroflex "la") isn't in Hindi. Hindi-trained OCR reads it as ल or drops it. *कोळी* becomes *कोली*. Marathi also uses ऱ and its own spellings that Hindi models "correct". We use OCR set up for Marathi and a person checks the names.

article.text: Manipur goes to the polls in early 2027, on a roll that was rebuilt in 2026.

That matters more here than almost anywhere. The Special Intensive Revision re-verified Manipur's voters house by house, and the final roll was scheduled for 6 September 2026. Whatever lists campaigns were working from before — the 2022 roll, the 2024 Lok Sabha roll — no longer line up with it.

items: entries for voters who died or were duplicated — removed

article.text: With an election a few months later, there's very little time to absorb all that. Opening 60 constituencies of scanned PDFs eats into it. A sheet doesn't.
Family Name First: How Meitei Names Work
Here's something generic converters get wrong. Meitei names traditionally put the family name first:
Laishram Ibomcha Singh — Laishram is the *yumnak*, the family name. Thokchom Sanatombi Devi — Thokchom is the family name.

Software built for "first name, last name" files these people under the wrong letter and splits families across the sort. We keep the printed order, so sorting by name puts each household together. Hill-district names — Naga and Kuki-Zo communities — follow their own patterns, and we keep those exactly as printed too.

Manipur's 60 seats split between the Imphal valley and the hill districts — Inner Manipur covers most of the valley, Outer Manipur the hills and the rest. Booth sizes, distances and name patterns differ a lot between the two. Every constituency file comes in the same format anyway, so a state team can compare them side by side.

article.text: Run a Meghalaya roll through ordinary OCR and it starts "correcting" people's names.

Khasi, Garo and Jaintia names include clan names software has never seen — Lyngdoh, Kharkongor, Sangma, Marak, Nongrum — and given names that are English words, chosen by parents for their meaning or sound. Spell-check-style tools see those and "fix" them into something more familiar. Then nobody can find that voter in a search.

article.text: Odisha holds its Assembly and Lok Sabha elections on the same day. One roll, two contests.

That changes how a campaign uses its voter list. The same booth sheet has to work for an assembly candidate and a Lok Sabha candidate — which means the data has to roll up cleanly from booth to constituency to Lok Sabha seat. Next time is 2029, and the roll it'll run on was rebuilt in 2026.
The Odisha voter list in Excel gives you that roll in a form that rolls up: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Odia, English and Hindi.
Odisha Votes Both Ballots at Once
Because both elections happen together, Odisha campaigns often coordinate across assembly and Lok Sabha teams. Clean data helps:

items: each of the 21 Lok Sabha seats is seven assembly segments — order one bundle and you have all seven
every workbook uses the same layout, so totals add up without rework
booth sheets can go to whichever team is working that ground
the summary sheets compare instantly across segments

article.text: Round Letters, Real Problems

Odia script is beautiful and a pain to read off a scan. Its letters are rounded, with few straight strokes, and on a low-resolution PDF several look nearly identical — ଠ, ଡ and ଢ are the classic trio. OCR trained on Devanagari or Bengali gets them wrong constantly.
We use OCR set up for Odia, a person checks the names, and every booth is matched against the official men and women totals before it ships. The English and Hindi transliterations get the same care.
(Sample row for illustration.)
The SIR 2026 Roll

Odisha was one of the first states to complete phase three of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers verified voters house to house, and the final roll was scheduled for 21 September 2026.

That roll removes deaths, duplicates and voters who shifted away — Odisha sends many workers to other states — and adds new voters who turned 18 by 1 July 2026. The 2024 roll no longer lines up booth for booth.

article.text: Punjab votes in early 2027. Its new voter roll lands in October 2026. That's a tight squeeze.

The Special Intensive Revision's final roll for Punjab was scheduled for 19 October 2026. A few months later, the state goes to the polls. Every booth plan, every pind-level worker list, every "who's new on the roll" check has to happen in that window — on the new roll, not the old one.
The Punjab voter list in Excel is built to make that window enough: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Punjabi, English and Hindi.
Early 2027 Means the Booth Work Is Now
What a campaign has to get done between the final roll and polling day:

items: See which voters SIR removed from each booth — and check them
Find every new voter added since 2022
Re-map booths that were split or renumbered
Hand each booth sheet to its worker
Track contact, booth by booth, through to polling day
Do it for every constituency you're fighting in

article.text: From PDFs, step one alone eats weeks. From a sheet, it's a filter.
2017 to 2022: More Voters, Fewer Showing Up
The last two elections tell a story worth planning around.

Punjab added 15.8 lakh voters and 2,125 polling stations between the two elections — and turnout fell five points. More people on the roll, fewer at the booth. That's the gap booth teams spend 2027 trying to close. And you can't close it without knowing who those voters are.
Source: Election Commission of India statistical reports, Punjab Assembly elections 2017 and 2022.
Kaur, Kour, Kor – and Other Gurmukhi Traps

Gurmukhi OCR stumbles on small marks. The tippi and bindi nasal signs vanish on a faint scan, and a name quietly changes. Then English spelling makes it worse: ਕੌਰ becomes *Kaur* in one booth, *Kour* in the next, *Kor* in a third. Search for one and you find a third of the women in the constituency.
We keep the Gurmukhi exactly as printed, pick one English spelling per name and use it consistently across the file, and add Hindi for teams from outside Punjab. A person checks every name.

article.text: In western Rajasthan, the next booth can be 30 kilometres of sand away.

Barmer, Jaisalmer, Bikaner — constituencies bigger than some countries, with dhanis (hamlets) scattered across the desert. A campaign vehicle that leaves with the wrong list doesn't just waste an hour. It wastes a day. Planning starts with knowing exactly who's on each booth's roll before the jeep leaves.
The Rajasthan voter list in Excel gives you that: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
In the Desert, Every Trip Has to Count
What desert-seat teams do with a sortable list that they can't do with PDFs:

items: sort each booth by section, so the route follows the hamlets in order
see booth sizes at a glance and send bigger teams to bigger booths
spot elderly voters who may need help to vote
check which households are new on the roll since 2023

article.text: Eastern Rajasthan — Jaipur, Alwar, Bharatpur — has the opposite problem: dense booths, lots of voters, tight streets. Same file, different use.
"Ram Lal" or "Ramlal"? The Spacing Problem

Here's a Rajasthan-specific annoyance. Compound names — Ram Lal / Ramlal, Shyam Sundar / Shyamsundar, Bhanwar Lal / Bhanwarlal — are written with and without the space, sometimes within the same booth. Search for one form and you miss the other.
Two fixes. We keep each name as printed in Hindi and make the English spelling consistent within your file. And in Excel, a "contains" filter on "Lal" or "Ram" catches both forms.
(Sample row for illustration.)
The SIR 2026 Roll

Rajasthan was in phase two of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers went door to door from November 2025, and the final roll was published on 21 February 2026. Deceased, shifted and duplicate entries came off, new voters were added, and some booths were split. The 2023 roll no longer lines up booth for booth — and 2028 will be fought on the new one.

article.text: Sikkim has an assembly seat with no boundaries.

The Sangha constituency isn't a place on a map. Its voters are the monks and nuns of Sikkim's registered monasteries, wherever those monasteries happen to be — Rumtek, Pemayangtse, Enchey, and dozens more across the hills. It's the only seat of its kind in India, and its voter list looks nothing like an ordinary constituency's.
The Sikkim voter list in Excel covers it, along with the other 31 seats: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names as printed plus Hindi.
The Only Assembly Seat Where Monks Are the Electorate
What makes the Sangha roll different:

items: voters are grouped by monastery, not by neighbourhood
booths can sit far apart, in different districts
names follow monastic and Buddhist naming traditions
a campaign here is about institutions, not streets

article.text: We keep every name exactly as printed and the booth structure intact, so the Sangha file is as usable as any other.
Small State, Unusual Reservations
Sikkim's 32 seats don't follow the usual General/SC/ST pattern:

article.text: Tamil Nadu's roll lost nearly 97 lakh names in one revision.

When the Special Intensive Revision's final roll came out on 23 February 2026, Tamil Nadu stood at about 5.67 crore voters — after one of the largest clean-ups of any state. Deaths, duplicates, people who'd moved to Chennai, Bengaluru or the Gulf and never updated their entry: gone. That's the roll the state voted on in 2026, and the one it'll be working from for years.
The Tamil Nadu voter list in Excel gives you that roll ready to use: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Tamil, English and Hindi.
97 Lakh Names Off the Roll
A clean-up that size changes everything downstream:

items: booth totals from 2021 or 2024 are meaningless now
turnout calculated on the old roll understated real participation
walk lists from earlier campaigns are full of people who aren't there
city seats — Chennai especially — saw the biggest churn
new voters added during claims are the ones nobody has a record of
booth renumbering means old part numbers point to the wrong lists

article.text: Throw out the old file. Seriously.
Initials Are the Real Surname

Most Tamil names don't have a surname in the North Indian sense. They have an initial — usually the father's name, sometimes father's and grandfather's — in front: R. Kumar, S. Lakshmi, K. P. Senthil.

That initial is how you tell two Kumars in the same booth apart. Cheap conversions drop it, or merge it into the name, or move it to the end. We keep it exactly as printed — and sorting by initial and relative's name groups families neatly.
Tamil to Hindi Is Not Letter for Letter
Tamil script uses one letter where Hindi uses several: க covers k, kh, g and gh. So a letter-by-letter Hindi transliteration of கணேசன் comes out as "कणेसन्" — wrong. The right Hindi is गणेशन.
We transliterate by the standard spelling of the name, not letter by letter, and a person checks it. English gets the same care: Karthik, Karthick and Kaarthik don't all become different people.

article.text: Tripura is the last state in line for its new roll. Its SIR final roll isn't due until 23 December 2026.

That leaves campaigns with a choice. Work on the current roll now and redo it in January — or prepare everything now and switch the week the new roll lands. We support both. Files from the current roll are available today, and we convert the SIR final roll as soon as it's published.
Either way, the Tripura voter list in Excel comes as one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Bengali, English and Hindi.
Last in Line for SIR – Here's What That Means
The phase three schedule for Tripura:

What changes when it lands: deceased voters and duplicates come off, shifted voters leave their old booths, new 18-year-olds are added, and booths over 1,200 voters get split. If you're using today's roll, plan for a full refresh in January — and budget a day to re-map booth workers, not a week.
Kokborok Names in Bengali Script

Tripura's roll is printed in Bengali. That works well for Bengali names. It works less well for Kokborok and other tribal names — Debbarma, Reang, Jamatia, Tripura, Halam — which are written in a script that wasn't built for them. The result: one name spelt several ways across booths, and OCR that struggles with the unusual letter combinations.

We keep each name in Bengali as printed, use one consistent English spelling per name across the file, and add Hindi for teams from outside the state. A person checks every booth against the official totals.

state.title: UP Voter List in Excel – SIR 2026 Roll for the 2027 Election
state.lead: Uttar Pradesh's SIR 2026 voter list in searchable Excel for all 403 constituencies, ready for the 2027 election. One booth per sheet, Hindi and English.

article.text: Uttar Pradesh votes in early 2027. That's 403 constituencies, every one of them on a rebuilt roll.

UP's Special Intensive Revision ran longer than any other state's in phase two — the final roll only came out on 10 April 2026. It's the roll the 2027 Assembly election will be fought on. And with 403 seats and 80 Lok Sabha constituencies, the sheer volume of it is the problem: hundreds of thousands of booth PDFs, all scanned Hindi, none of it searchable.
The UP voter list in Excel turns that into data you can actually run a campaign on: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
403 Seats, One Year to Go
What a UP campaign has to get through before polling day, constituency by constituency:

items: Compare the SIR roll against the 2022 roll and see who's gone
Find the new voters added since then
Re-map booths that were split or renumbered
Size every booth and assign workers in proportion
Print walk lists by section and house number
Track contact, booth by booth, right up to polling day
Roll it all up to Lok Sabha seats and regions

article.text: Seven steps, 403 times. From PDFs, that's not a plan. It's a wish.
What SIR 2026 Did to UP's Roll

Booth Level Officers verified voters house to house from November 2025. The draft removed large numbers of deceased, shifted and duplicate entries. Then the claims period added many names back — new voters and people who had been missed. The final roll in April 2026 is the result.

UP sends huge numbers of workers to Delhi, Mumbai, Punjab, Gujarat and the Gulf. That made the "shifted" category big here — and it's why a 2022 walk list now sends volunteers looking for people who left years ago.
Hindi Names at UP Scale

The roll is in Hindi, and at UP's scale small OCR errors add up fast. Matras blur on faded scans, ि and ी swap, and the same name gets written several ways across a constituency. Multiply that by 403 seats and a state team's search tools stop working.
We keep each name in Hindi with one consistent spelling and add an English transliteration, checked by a person, so the files load cleanly into CRMs, dashboards and campaign apps.

state.lead: West Bengal's SIR 2026 voter list in searchable Excel for all 294 constituencies. One booth per sheet, names in Bengali, English and Hindi.

article.text: Search a Bengal voter list for "Banerjee" and half the Banerjees won't show up.

They're on the roll as Bandyopadhyay — the full Bengali form. Same story with Chatterjee and Chattopadhyay, Mukherjee and Mukhopadhyay, Ganguly and Gangopadhyay. Both versions are in everyday use, and the roll prints whichever the voter registered with. A campaign office that doesn't know this will swear voters are "missing".
The West Bengal voter list in Excel keeps every name as printed and makes it easy to find: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Bengali, English and Hindi.
Banerjee or Bandyopadhyay? Both Are on the Roll
How to search a Bengal file without losing people:

items: search both the short and the full surname
or search the Bengali column — বন্দ্যোপাধ্যায় and ব্যানার্জী are distinct there too, but at least you know what you're looking at
use a "contains" filter on a stem — "Banerj" or "Bandyo"
sort by surname, then relative's name, to group households

article.text: We transliterate exactly what's printed, keep the spelling consistent within your file, and don't silently "standardise" names — that would hide what's actually on the roll.
The SIR 2026 Roll

West Bengal was in phase two of the Special Intensive Revision, one of the most closely watched anywhere. Booth Level Officers verified voters house to house from November 2025, and the final roll was published on 28 February 2026 — the roll the state then voted on.

Deceased, shifted and duplicate entries came off; new voters were added; booths were split where they crossed 1,200 voters. Data from the 2021 election or the 2024 Lok Sabha poll doesn't line up booth for booth anymore.
Kolkata, the Hills and Everything Between
294 seats cover very different ground:

items: Kolkata and its suburbs — dense booths, heavy rental churn
North Bengal and the Darjeeling hills — Nepali names alongside Bengali ones, printed in Bengali script
Jangalmahal and the western districts — tribal names with no fixed English spelling
The border districts — large booths, long distances

article.text: The next Chhattisgarh Assembly election is in 2028. The booth work starts now.

That's not campaign-consultant hype. Chhattisgarh's roll was rebuilt in the Special Intensive Revision, with the final version out on 21 February 2026 — and it will be the base for every revision until polling day. Teams that map their booths on it early walk into 2028 knowing their ground. Teams that wait inherit a scramble.
The Chhattisgarh voter list in Excel gives you that base: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
Two Years Out Is When Booth Work Actually Gets Done

Ask anyone who has run a booth committee. The final month before polling is for turnout. The real groundwork — knowing which family lives where, which young voters are new on the roll, which booth has twice the voters of its neighbour — happens years earlier.
You can't do that from 90 constituencies' worth of scanned PDFs. You can do it in an afternoon with a sheet you can sort.
What SIR 2026 Changed
Chhattisgarh was in phase two of SIR, alongside eleven other states and UTs. Booth Level Officers went door to door from November 2025. By February 2026:

items: dead, shifted and duplicate entries were removed
new voters were added through claims
booth lists were tidied, and some renumbered
the 2023 election roll stopped matching the current one booth for booth

article.text: 29 Tribal Seats, Thousands of Remote Booths

Twenty-nine of Chhattisgarh's 90 seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribe candidates — the Bastar division in the south, Surguja in the north, and the forest belts in between. Booths here can be small, far apart and hard to reach.

That changes what a voter list is for. In a dense city booth, you're managing volume. In a forest-belt booth, you're making sure a single trip covers every household. A sheet sorted by section and house number is the difference between one visit and three.
Hindi Names, Cleaned Up
The roll is in Hindi, and the scans are where things go wrong. OCR blurs matras, swaps ि and ी, and spells the same name three ways across three booths. Search falls apart fast.
We keep every name in Hindi with one consistent spelling and add an English transliteration, reviewed by a person, so the file works in software that can't handle Devanagari.

article.text: Jharkhand's rebuilt voter list is days away. Be ready to open it the morning it lands.

The Special Intensive Revision's final roll for Jharkhand was scheduled for 7 October 2026. Booth Level Officers spent the summer verifying every household; the draft went out in August; claims ran through September. The result will be the most accurate Jharkhand roll in years — and the old one stops being useful the day it's published.
The Jharkhand voter list in Excel turns the new roll into something your team can actually use: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
The Final Roll Lands This Month
What a full SIR does to a state's data:

items: people who died — removed
workers who moved permanently to other states and re-registered — removed from their old booth
duplicates — cleaned out
new voters who turned 18 by the qualifying date — added
polling stations over the 1,200-voter limit — split and renumbered
every booth list from 2024 — out of sync

article.text: Jharkhand sends a lot of workers to other states. That makes the "shifted" category big here, and it's exactly why old lists send volunteers looking for people who left years ago.

article.text: In Uttarakhand's hills, whole villages have emptied out. The voter roll is only now catching up.

Pauri, Almora, Tehri, Pithoragarh — for years, people have left the hills for Dehradun, Haldwani, Delhi and beyond. Many stayed registered at the family house they'd left. So hill booth lists carried names of people who hadn't lived there in a decade, while plains booths in Dehradun and Udham Singh Nagar kept swelling.

The Special Intensive Revision fixed a lot of that. Uttarakhand's final roll was scheduled for 15 September 2026, a few months before the 2027 election. The Uttarakhand voter list in Excel gives it to you ready to use: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
Hill Booths Shrank. Plains Booths Grew.
What SIR does to a state with this much internal migration:

items: hill booths lose voters who had permanently shifted
plains and city booths gain new residents who enrolled where they actually live
booths over 1,200 voters in fast-growing areas get split and renumbered
the 2022 roll stops being a guide to who actually votes where

article.text: For a campaign, the takeaway is blunt. In hill seats, your 2022 voter count overstated the real electorate. In plains seats, it understated it. Re-size every booth on the new roll before you assign a single worker.
A Few Months From Roll to Vote

Final roll in September. Election due early 2027. In between: booth committees, walk lists, worker allocation, new-voter outreach — across 70 seats, many of them reachable only by mountain roads that close in winter.
A sortable sheet saves weeks in that window. Sort a hill booth by section and house number, and a worker can cover it in one trip instead of three.

article.text: Hyderabad's voter list was out of date the day it was printed.

Gachibowli, Madhapur, Kukatpally, the old city, the new tech corridors: people rent, move, switch jobs, move again. Many never touch their voter registration. So until now, a Hyderabad booth list has been part roll, part ghost town. The Special Intensive Revision is the first real reset in years — and Telangana's final roll was scheduled for 19 October 2026.
The Telangana voter list in Excel gives you that reset in a usable form: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Telugu, English and Hindi.
Hyderabad Is a Moving Target
A rough picture of what SIR does to a city seat:

items: tenants who moved out years ago — removed as shifted
voters registered at both their old and new addresses — duplicates cleaned out
people who moved in and enrolled during the revision — added
crowded booths over the 1,200-voter cap — split and renumbered

article.text: Rural Telangana sees the same changes, just smaller. In the city, the difference between the 2023 roll and the 2026 one is big enough that old booth data is basically fiction.
The SIR 2026 Final Roll

Telangana is in phase three. The draft roll came out on 10 August 2026, claims and objections followed, and the final roll was scheduled for 19 October 2026, with 1 October 2026 as the qualifying date. Our files use the final roll.
Telugu, Urdu-Origin and English Names in One File
Telangana's roll is in Telugu, but its names come from several traditions — and each trips up software differently.
Telugu names put the family name first: *Gaddam Ravi Kumar*, where Gaddam is the family name. We keep the printed order so households sort together.
Urdu-origin names written in Telugu script — common in Hyderabad — have no fixed English spelling. Mohammed, Mohd., Muhammad. We pick one consistent spelling per name across the file.
Telugu script itself — rounded letters and stacked consonant clusters — smears on scans. Every booth is checked against the official men and women totals.

state.lead: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands SIR 2026 voter list in searchable Excel. One booth per sheet across every island, names in English and Hindi.

article.text: In the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, some booths are a ship's voyage apart.

The UT stretches more than 700 kilometres from north to south, across dozens of inhabited islands — from Diglipur in North Andaman down to Campbell Bay on Great Nicobar. A campaign can't hop between booths on a whim. Every trip is planned around ferry schedules, and every visit has to count.
The Andaman & Nicobar voter list in Excel gives you every booth in one file: one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in English and Hindi.
Booths You Reach by Boat
When the next booth means the next ferry, a sortable list changes how you plan:

items: group booths by island and plan one voyage per group
see which booths have the most voters and send people there first
sort each booth by section and house number before you sail
flag first-time and elderly voters with a filter

article.text: Names From Every Corner of India

The islands were settled over generations from all over the country — Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand and more — alongside the Nicobarese and other island communities. Walk through one booth list and you'll find Bengali, Tamil, Malayalam, Telugu and Nicobarese names next to each other.
Generic OCR handles some of those and mangles others. We keep every name exactly as printed and add a Hindi column, checked by a person.
(Sample row for illustration.)
The SIR 2026 Roll

Andaman & Nicobar was in phase two of the Special Intensive Revision. Booth Level Officers verified voters across the islands, and the final roll was published on 21 February 2026. Our files use it, with supplementary lists merged in.

A summary sheet: every booth, polling station, and men, women and third-gender totals
One row per voter: EPIC number, name, relative's name, relation, house number, age, gender, section

state.title: Chandigarh Voter List in Excel – SIR 2026 Roll, Booth-Wise
state.lead: Chandigarh's SIR 2026 voter list in searchable Excel. One booth per sheet, sector-wise house numbers kept intact, names in English and Hindi.

article.text: Chandigarh is laid out in neat numbered sectors. Its voter list, in PDF form, is anything but neat.

Every address in the city follows a pattern — House No. 1234, Sector 22-B — that should make door-to-door work easy. In a scanned PDF you can't sort by any of it. And paste it into Excel carelessly and "22-B" or "1234/2" gets mangled into something else entirely.
The Chandigarh voter list in Excel keeps those addresses exactly as printed, stored as text: one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in English and Hindi.
A Planned City Deserves a Planned List
What you can do once sectors and house numbers are clean:

items: filter a booth to one sector
sort by house number and walk the street in order
compare voters across sectors and villages in one sheet
hand each worker exactly the houses they cover

article.text: Chandigarh's villages and colonies — Burail, Maloya, Dhanas, Mauli Jagran and others — have messier addresses. We keep those exactly as printed too.
Municipal Polls Come First

For Chandigarh campaigns, the next big contest is usually the Municipal Corporation election, not the Lok Sabha. Those polls run on ward-wise rolls from the State Election Commission, not the Lok Sabha roll. We convert ward rolls on request — tell us the wards and we'll quote.
The SIR 2026 Roll

Chandigarh was in phase three of the Special Intensive Revision. The final roll was scheduled for 22 September 2026, with 1 July 2026 as the qualifying date. A city with this many students, government transfers and tenants sees a lot of churn — SIR removed many voters who had moved and added new residents.

article.text: This UT is three places that aren't next to each other.

Dadra & Nagar Haveli sits inland between Gujarat and Maharashtra. Daman is on the Gujarat coast. Diu is an island off Saurashtra, a long drive away from both. Since the 2020 merger they're one Union Territory — but they still elect two separate MPs, and campaigns treat them as separate ground.
The Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu voter list in Excel follows that split: one workbook per Lok Sabha seat, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names as printed plus English and Hindi.
One UT, Three Places, Two Seats
Order one seat or both. Diu booths can be split out if your team only works the island.
Silvassa's Shifting Workforce

Dadra & Nagar Haveli's industrial estates around Silvassa employ large numbers of workers from across India. They move between jobs, flats and states often — and voter registrations lag behind. Meanwhile the tribal villages of Nagar Haveli have long-settled families with their own naming patterns.
That mix makes the roll churn in some booths and stay rock-steady in others. SIR caught up on a lot of it. In Silvassa especially, plan on the new roll.

article.text: Paste a Delhi voter list into Excel and it quietly turns house number "3/4" into the 3rd of April.

It's one of those bugs nobody notices until a volunteer turns up at the wrong door. Delhi addresses are full of slashes and dashes — RZ-45/2, WZ-112A, C-3/14, H.No. 12-1, Gali No. 3 — and Excel helpfully "fixes" a good share of them into dates. Sort that column and the walk list is garbage.

Our files store every house number as text, exactly as printed. The Delhi voter list in Excel comes as one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Hindi and English.
RZ-45/2, Gali No. 3: Delhi's Addresses Break Excel
What goes wrong when Delhi rolls are converted carelessly:

items: "3/4" becomes 03-Apr
"12-1" becomes 12-Jan
leading zeros vanish — "045" turns into 45
block prefixes like RZ and WZ get split into a separate column

article.text: Small things. They wreck the one job a door-to-door team needs the list for. So the house column stays text, untouched, and you can sort by it safely.
A City That Moves Every Lease Cycle

Delhi's population turns over constantly. Tenants in Laxmi Nagar, Mukherjee Nagar, Uttam Nagar and the urban villages move every year or two; families shift between colonies; whole unauthorised colonies grow between elections. A lot of those moves never reach the voter roll.
The Special Intensive Revision is the reset. Expect the biggest changes in seats with lots of rented housing — and expect 2025 election booth data to be well out of date there.

state.title: Lakshadweep Voter List in Excel – SIR 2026, Every Island
state.lead: Lakshadweep's SIR 2026 voter list in searchable Excel. Every inhabited island, one booth per sheet, Malayalam names plus English and Hindi.

article.text: Lakshadweep has the smallest electorate of any Lok Sabha seat in India. It's also one of the hardest to cover.

Its voters live on ten inhabited islands scattered across the Arabian Sea — Kavaratti, Agatti, Amini, Andrott, Kalpeni, Kadmat, Kiltan, Chetlat, Bitra and Minicoy. Moving between them means boats and schedules. With a voter base this small, every household matters, and every trip has to be planned.
The Lakshadweep voter list in Excel puts the whole UT in one place: one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, in Malayalam, English and Hindi.
India's Smallest Electorate, Spread Across the Sea
What island-by-island planning looks like with a sortable list:

items: group booths by island and plan one crossing per island
see voter counts per island before deciding where to spend time
sort each booth by house name and walk it in order
flag first-time voters in every island with one filter

article.text: When the whole seat is a few tens of thousands of voters, a few hundred votes on one island can decide it.
House Names and Malayalam Script

Lakshadweep's roll is printed in Malayalam, and like Kerala's, it often records house names rather than numbers. Those names are how islanders identify families. We keep them, in their own column, exactly as printed.

Minicoy is different again — its people speak Mahl, though the roll still uses Malayalam script. Names here have their own spellings, and we check every one by hand. Malayalam's chillu letters (ൽ, ൻ, ർ) are the usual OCR trap, and every booth is matched against the official men and women totals.

article.text: Puducherry is the only place in India where one small UT needs three different scripts to read its voter list.

It's four regions, hundreds of kilometres apart. Puducherry and Karaikal sit on the Tamil Nadu coast and use Tamil. Mahe is a tiny enclave inside Kerala and uses Malayalam. Yanam is surrounded by Andhra Pradesh and uses Telugu. One UT, one Lok Sabha seat, three scripts — and most converters can handle one of them at best.
The Puducherry voter list in Excel handles all three: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in the original script plus English and Hindi.
One UT, Four Regions, Three Scripts
A UT-wide campaign team ends up juggling all three. The English and Hindi columns give everyone a common script to work in, whatever region they're looking at.
Why Mixed-Script Rolls Break Converters
Each script has its own traps, and we've hit every one:

items: Tamil names carry an initial instead of a surname — R. Kumar — and the initial must not be dropped
Malayalam has chillu letters (ൽ, ൻ, ർ) that OCR misreads, and Mahe rolls often list house names
Telugu puts the family name first and stacks consonants that smear on scans
Tamil to Hindi isn't letter for letter: கணேசன் should become गणेशन, not "कणेसन्"

article.text: Any Jammu & Kashmir voter data from before 2022 is mapped to seats that no longer exist.

The 2022 delimitation redrew J&K from scratch. Assembly seats went from 83 to 90 — 47 in the Kashmir division, 43 in Jammu. Boundaries moved. Nine seats were reserved for Scheduled Tribes for the first time. The Lok Sabha map changed too, with a brand-new Anantnag-Rajouri seat stretching across the Pir Panjal. The 2024 Assembly election, the first in a decade, was fought on that new map.
The Jammu & Kashmir voter list in Excel follows it: one workbook per constituency, one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, with names as printed plus English and Hindi where needed.
New Map, New Seats, New Lok Sabha Lines
What the delimitation broke for anyone holding older data:

items: constituency totals from 2014 cover different ground
seven new seats didn't exist before
ST reservation applies to nine seats for the first time
Lok Sabha segments were reshuffled — each seat now has 18
booths moved between constituencies
old booth-wise analysis lands in the wrong seat

article.text: Patching an old file to the new map is a slow, error-prone job. Start from the current roll.
One Name, Five English Spellings

Names here have more English variants than almost anywhere. Mohammad, Mohammed, Mohd., Muhammad, Md. — all one name, and all likely to appear in the same constituency. Kashmiri and Dogri names add their own variations, and Urdu-script entries often leave out short vowels.

We keep each name as printed and pick one consistent English spelling per name across your file, so a single search finds everyone. A Hindi column helps teams in the Jammu division who read Devanagari faster.

state.lead: Ladakh's voter list in searchable Excel for the whole UT – Leh and Kargil, booth by booth. One booth per sheet, names in English and Hindi.

article.text: Ladakh is India's biggest Lok Sabha seat by area — and one of its smallest by voters.

Its booths are scattered across high deserts, river valleys and passes that close for months: Changthang, Nubra, Zanskar, Drass, Suru. Some polling stations serve a handful of nomadic families. Reaching them is the hard part. Knowing who's on each list shouldn't be.
The Ladakh voter list in Excel covers the whole UT: one sheet per booth, every voter on one row, names in English and Hindi.
The Highest, Emptiest Booths in India
With voters this spread out, a campaign plans around geography first:

items: group booths by valley and plan one trip per valley
see which booths are tiny and which carry real numbers
sort each booth by section and house before the vehicle leaves
spot first-time voters and elderly voters with one filter

article.text: A wasted trip in Ladakh can cost days. The list is the cheapest thing to get right.
Leh and Kargil Are Different Campaigns

Ladakh's two districts often vote very differently, and each has its own Autonomous Hill Development Council with its own elections. Campaign teams usually split along those lines. We can deliver Leh and Kargil booths as separate workbooks, so each team gets only its ground.
Names here follow several traditions, and generic OCR handles some of them badly. We keep every name exactly as printed and add Hindi, checked by a person.
(Sample row for illustration.)
Which Roll This Is

Ladakh was not included in the first three phases of the Special Intensive Revision. Our files use the latest final roll published by the CEO, with supplementary lists merged in. The roll date is printed on every sheet.
